prompt: rust futures select_next_some behavior with None
answer:
`select_next_some()` skips `None` items: the corresponding `select!` branch does not run. It only runs when the stream yields `Some(value)`. [Async Book](https://rust-lang.github.io/async-book/06_multiple_futures/03_select.html)

When the stream is exhausted, `select_next_some()` is considered terminated. Used inside the `select!` macro, the fused-future handling prevents it from being polled again; once all branches are terminated, the `complete` branch runs. [API documentation](https://rust-lang-nursery.github.io/futures-api-docs/0.1.27/futures_util/stream/trait.StreamExt.html)

Polling `select_next_some()` directly after the stream is empty can panic. It requires a `FusedStream + Unpin`, and the stream must correctly report termination.
